Deep Learning CA2 Part A¶

GAN vs VAE Comparison and Final Selection¶

This notebook is the final integration and evaluation stage of the CIFAR-10 generative-modelling project.

The GAN and VAE development programmes are complete before this notebook begins. Their selected architectures, hyperparameters and checkpoints are frozen. This notebook verifies the frozen artifacts, defines one common final-evaluation protocol, performs the protected held-out comparison, selects the overall model, and generates the official 1,000-image submission set.

No model training or tuning is performed here.

1. Notebook Overview and Frozen-Model Boundary¶

1.1 Purpose¶

This notebook has five main responsibilities:

  1. independently reconstruct and verify the frozen final GAN and VAE;
  2. freeze one fair final-evaluation protocol before protected-test evaluation begins;
  3. compare both models using held-out, blind-human and memorisation evidence;
  4. select and freeze the overall GAN-versus-VAE winner;
  5. generate exactly 1,000 final CIFAR-10 images, with 100 requested samples per class, and verify the saved deliverable at file level.

The modelling phase is closed. No architecture, hyperparameter, augmentation, conditioning, checkpoint or training-seed decision will be reopened in this notebook.

1.2 Relationship to Notebooks 1–3¶

Notebook Main responsibility Status entering Notebook 4
Notebook 1 CIFAR-10 EDA, preprocessing, shared representation, grayscale and augmentation context Complete
Notebook 2 GAN development, controlled experiments, within-family selection and final GAN freeze Complete and frozen
Notebook 3 VAE development, controlled experiments, within-family selection and final VAE freeze Complete and frozen
Notebook 4 Frozen-model verification, final shared evaluation, cross-model selection and official generation Current notebook

Notebook 4 reuses the decisions and valid development evidence from the earlier notebooks rather than repeating their experiments.

1.3 Final Data-Use and No-Tuning Policy¶

The official CIFAR-10 test set was not used to train, tune, select or revise either final generative model.

The final GAN and VAE enter this notebook as frozen artifacts. Before the protected test set is accessed, this notebook must:

  • independently reload both frozen generation networks;
  • verify their expected input and output interfaces;
  • verify conversion into the shared RGB uint8 [0,255] representation;
  • write and freeze the complete final-evaluation protocol.

After protected-test evaluation begins:

  • no retraining is allowed;
  • no checkpoint or model reselection is allowed;
  • no hyperparameter or architecture change is allowed;
  • no outcome-driven evaluation-protocol change is allowed.

A genuine implementation error may be corrected transparently, but any affected comparison must then be rerun symmetrically.

2. Environment, Data and Frozen Artifact Verification¶

This section verifies that the exact frozen GAN generator and VAE decoder can be reconstructed and used correctly before the protected final-evaluation protocol is activated.

No CIFAR-10 test images are loaded or evaluated in this section.

2.1 Environment and Reproducibility¶

The final comparison uses a lightweight notebook-local setup. Environment versions are recorded for reproducibility, while the final evaluation seeds and sample counts remain pending until the Section 3 protocol is approved and frozen.

The seed used in this section is only for artifact-verification samples. It is not a final evaluation seed.

2.2 CIFAR-10 Contract and Protected-Test Firewall¶

Notebook 1 established the common CIFAR-10 data contract:

  • 50,000 official training images;
  • 10,000 official test images;
  • RGB images with shape 32 × 32 × 3;
  • original storage as uint8 [0,255];
  • fixed class labels 0 to 9;
  • fixed class order from Airplane to Truck.

For the stricter final-evaluation firewall used in this notebook, the actual CIFAR-10 loader is deliberately not called yet. The Keras loader returns both training and test data together, so loading it here would access the protected test set before the complete Section 3 protocol is frozen.

The official dataset will therefore be loaded and validated only after Section 3 has been approved and the protected-test gate has opened.

This section only verifies the inherited representation contract and the inverse conversions required for frozen-model outputs.

In [2]:

assert len(CLASS_NAMES) == NUM_CLASSES

def restore_from_gan(images):
    """Convert GAN outputs from approximately [-1, 1] to uint8 [0, 255]."""
    restored = (np.asarray(images) + 1.0) * 127.5
    return np.clip(
        np.rint(restored),
        0,
        255,
    ).astype("uint8")


def restore_from_vae(images):
    """Convert VAE outputs from [0, 1] to uint8 [0, 255]."""
    restored = np.asarray(images) * 255.0
    return np.clip(
        np.rint(restored),
        0,
        255,
    ).astype("uint8")


# Boundary checks for the inherited conversions.
assert np.array_equal(
    restore_from_gan(
        np.array([-1.0, 1.0], dtype=np.float32)
    ),
    np.array([0, 255], dtype=np.uint8),
)

assert np.array_equal(
    restore_from_vae(
        np.array([0.0, 1.0], dtype=np.float32)
    ),
    np.array([0, 255], dtype=np.uint8),
)

2.3 Final GAN Reload Verification¶

Notebook 2 selected and froze G10_conditional_fliptranslation_seed42 at epoch 100.

The final generator uses:

  • latent dimension 100;
  • integer requested-class labels with shape (N,1);
  • a learned label embedding of dimension 50;
  • RGB output with shape 32 × 32 × 3;
  • tanh output activation, producing values approximately in [-1,1];
  • 1,290,487 generator parameters.

A fresh generator is reconstructed below from the final Notebook 2 architecture and loaded from the frozen .h5 weights. Only a small balanced inference batch is generated. This is an artifact-verification step, not final evaluation.

In [3]:
def build_final_gan_generator(
    latent_dim=GAN_LATENT_DIM,
    num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    label_embedding_dim=GAN_LABEL_EMBEDDING_DIM,
):
    weight_init = initializers.RandomNormal(
        mean=0.0,
        stddev=0.02,
    )

    noise_input = layers.Input(
        shape=(latent_dim,),
        name="conditional_noise_input",
    )

    label_input = layers.Input(
        shape=(1,),
        dtype="int32",
        name="conditional_generator_label",
    )

    label_embedding = layers.Embedding(
        input_dim=num_classes,
        output_dim=label_embedding_dim,
        embeddings_initializer=weight_init,
        name="generator_label_embedding",
    )(label_input)

    label_embedding = layers.Flatten(
        name="generator_label_flatten"
    )(label_embedding)

    x = layers.Concatenate(
        name="generator_conditioning_concatenation"
    )(
        [
            noise_input,
            label_embedding,
        ]
    )

    x = layers.Dense(
        4 * 4 * 256,
        use_bias=False,
        kernel_initializer=weight_init,
    )(x)

    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2)(x)
    x = layers.Reshape((4, 4, 256))(x)

    x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        128,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        use_bias=False,
        kernel_initializer=weight_init,
    )(x)

    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2)(x)

    x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        64,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        use_bias=False,
        kernel_initializer=weight_init,
    )(x)

    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2)(x)

    generated_image = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        3,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        activation="tanh",
        kernel_initializer=weight_init,
        name="conditional_generated_image",
    )(x)

    return keras.Model(
        inputs=[
            noise_input,
            label_input,
        ],
        outputs=generated_image,
        name="Conditional_DCGAN_Generator",
    )


assert GAN_GENERATOR_WEIGHTS_PATH.is_file(), (
    "Frozen GAN generator weights were not found at:\n"
    f"{GAN_GENERATOR_WEIGHTS_PATH}"
)

final_gan_generator = build_final_gan_generator()

assert (
    final_gan_generator.count_params()
    == EXPECTED_GAN_GENERATOR_PARAMS
)

final_gan_generator.load_weights(
    str(GAN_GENERATOR_WEIGHTS_PATH)
)

# One requested sample per CIFAR-10 class.
gan_verification_labels = tf.reshape(
    tf.range(NUM_CLASSES, dtype=tf.int32),
    (-1, 1),
)

gan_verification_noise = tf.random.stateless_normal(
    shape=(NUM_CLASSES, GAN_LATENT_DIM),
    seed=(ARTIFACT_VERIFICATION_SEED, 42),
)

gan_native_images = final_gan_generator(
    [
        gan_verification_noise,
        gan_verification_labels,
    ],
    training=False,
).numpy()

assert gan_native_images.shape == (
    NUM_CLASSES,
    32,
    32,
    3,
)

assert np.isfinite(gan_native_images).all()
assert gan_native_images.min() >= -1.0001
assert gan_native_images.max() <= 1.0001

gan_uint8_images = restore_from_gan(
    gan_native_images
)

assert gan_uint8_images.shape == (
    NUM_CLASSES,
    32,
    32,
    3,
)
assert gan_uint8_images.dtype == np.uint8

2.4 Final VAE Reload Verification¶

Notebook 3 exported a standalone frozen decoder model as VAE_FINAL_V04_decoder.keras.

The artifact was created under the legacy Keras environment used for Notebook 3 and is physically stored as an HDF5 whole-model file despite its .keras filename. Modern Keras reserves .keras for its newer native ZIP-based format. Therefore, Notebook 4 preserves the original artifact unchanged and creates a temporary .h5 compatibility copy in the runtime before loading it for inference.

No weights are modified and no VAE training occurs in this notebook.

In [4]:
import json
import shutil
import h5py

assert VAE_DECODER_MODEL_PATH.is_file(), (
    "Frozen V04 standalone decoder was not found at:\n"
    f"{VAE_DECODER_MODEL_PATH}"
)

assert h5py.is_hdf5(str(VAE_DECODER_MODEL_PATH)), (
    "Expected the supplied V04 decoder to be a legacy HDF5 model."
)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# Legacy Keras 2 -> Keras 3 compatibility copy
# -------------------------------------------------------
#
# Notebook 3 saved the decoder under Keras 2.x.
# Its serialized Conv2DTranspose configuration contains
# the legacy field `groups=1`, even though the original
# V04 architecture did not specify grouped transposed
# convolution.
#
# Current Keras Conv2DTranspose does not accept `groups`.
# Patch only that stale configuration field in a temporary
# runtime copy. The original frozen artifact remains unchanged.
# -------------------------------------------------------

VAE_DECODER_COMPAT_PATH = Path(
    "/tmp/VAE_FINAL_V04_decoder_compat.h5"
)

shutil.copy2(
    VAE_DECODER_MODEL_PATH,
    VAE_DECODER_COMPAT_PATH,
)


def remove_legacy_convtranspose_groups(config):
    """Remove only legacy groups=1 from Conv2DTranspose configs."""
    patched_count = 0

    if isinstance(config, dict):
        if (
            config.get("class_name") == "Conv2DTranspose"
            and isinstance(config.get("config"), dict)
            and "groups" in config["config"]
        ):
            groups_value = config["config"]["groups"]

            assert groups_value == 1, (
                "Unexpected grouped Conv2DTranspose found. "
                f"groups={groups_value}"
            )

            del config["config"]["groups"]
            patched_count += 1

        for value in config.values():
            patched_count += remove_legacy_convtranspose_groups(
                value
            )

    elif isinstance(config, list):
        for value in config:
            patched_count += remove_legacy_convtranspose_groups(
                value
            )

    return patched_count


with h5py.File(
    VAE_DECODER_COMPAT_PATH,
    "r+",
) as h5_file:

    assert "model_config" in h5_file.attrs, (
        "Legacy model does not contain model_config."
    )

    raw_model_config = h5_file.attrs[
        "model_config"
    ]

    if isinstance(raw_model_config, bytes):
        raw_model_config = raw_model_config.decode(
            "utf-8"
        )

    model_config = json.loads(
        raw_model_config
    )

    patched_layer_count = (
        remove_legacy_convtranspose_groups(
            model_config
        )
    )

    assert patched_layer_count == 3, (
        "Expected exactly three V04 Conv2DTranspose "
        "layers to require the legacy compatibility patch, "
        f"but found {patched_layer_count}."
    )

    h5_file.attrs["model_config"] = json.dumps(
        model_config
    )


print(
    "Legacy Conv2DTranspose configs patched:",
    patched_layer_count,
)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# Load the frozen decoder
# -------------------------------------------------------

final_vae_decoder = keras.models.load_model(
    str(VAE_DECODER_COMPAT_PATH),
    compile=False,
)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# Frozen decoder verification
# -------------------------------------------------------

assert (
    final_vae_decoder.count_params()
    == EXPECTED_VAE_DECODER_PARAMS
)

assert len(final_vae_decoder.inputs) == 2

assert tuple(
    final_vae_decoder.inputs[0].shape[1:]
) == (VAE_LATENT_DIM,)

assert tuple(
    final_vae_decoder.inputs[1].shape[1:]
) == (NUM_CLASSES,)

# One deterministic verification sample per class.
vae_verification_label_ids = tf.range(
    NUM_CLASSES,
    dtype=tf.int32,
)

vae_verification_labels = tf.one_hot(
    vae_verification_label_ids,
    depth=NUM_CLASSES,
    dtype=tf.float32,

vae_verification_latents = tf.random.stateless_normal(
    shape=(
        NUM_CLASSES,

    seed=(
        ARTIFACT_VERIFICATION_SEED,
        64,

vae_native_images = final_vae_decoder(

2.5 Shared RGB Evaluation Representation¶

Although the two frozen models use different native numerical ranges, their outputs are converted before any shared evaluation.

The common representation is:

shape  = (N, 32, 32, 3)
colour = RGB
dtype  = uint8
range  = [0,255]

The GAN uses the inherited inverse transformation from [-1,1], while the VAE uses the inherited inverse transformation from [0,1].

The real CIFAR-10 arrays will be checked against the same representation after the Section 3 protocol has been frozen and protected-test access becomes permitted.

In [5]:
def verify_shared_image_representation(
    name,
    images,
):
    assert isinstance(images, np.ndarray)
    assert images.ndim == 4
    assert images.shape[1:] == (32, 32, 3)
    assert images.dtype == np.uint8
    assert images.min() >= 0
    assert images.max() <= 255

    return {
        "Source": name,
        "Shape": str(images.shape),
        "dtype": str(images.dtype),
        "Minimum": int(images.min()),
        "Maximum": int(images.max()),
        "Status": "PASS",
    }


representation_rows = [
    verify_shared_image_representation(
        "Frozen GAN",
        gan_uint8_images,
    ),
    verify_shared_image_representation(
        "Frozen VAE",
        vae_uint8_images,
    ),
]

representation_table = pd.DataFrame(
    representation_rows
)

display(representation_table)

SHARED_GENERATED_REPRESENTATION_VERIFIED = True

print(
    "Generated-image shared representation: PASS"
)
print(
    "Real CIFAR-10 representation: "
    "DEFERRED until Section 3 protocol freeze"
)

2.6 Freeze-Gate Audit¶

3. Final Shared Evaluation Protocol¶

Before any protected-test result is produced, the final comparison protocol is written and frozen.

This prevents the official CIFAR-10 test set from influencing model selection, sampling choices, evaluation settings, or interpretation thresholds.

Both frozen models will be evaluated as fairly as possible using the same:

  • real-image reference where applicable;
  • RGB uint8 [0,255] representation;
  • generated sample counts;
  • requested-class balance;
  • feature extractor and preprocessing;
  • human-scoring definitions;
  • memorisation representation and nearest-neighbour procedure.

Model-specific evidence from earlier notebooks remains valid supporting evidence, but Notebook 4 will not rerun old analyses merely to force artificial symmetry between the GAN and VAE.

3.1 Protected-Test FID Protocol¶

Final FID uses the official CIFAR-10 test split only as an unseen real-image reference.

The protocol is:

  • real reference: all 10,000 official CIFAR-10 test images;
  • generated images per model per repeat: 5,000;
  • requested class balance: 500 images per class;
  • repeats: 3;
  • generation seeds: 2001, 2002, 2003;
  • feature extractor: frozen ImageNet InceptionV3;
  • feature layer: global average pooling;
  • feature dimension: 2,048;
  • identical resizing and Inception preprocessing for real, GAN and VAE images.

The same repeat seeds and evaluation implementation will be used for both frozen models.

For each model, report the three FID values, mean, standard deviation and sample count.

The repeated FID standard deviation represents generated-sample variability for the already-frozen model. It is not training-run uncertainty.

No formal cross-model FID threshold is used. In particular, the 2.0 practical FID margin used during GAN development is not transferred to this final GAN-versus-VAE comparison because it was calibrated for a different source of variation.

FID is therefore one important final evidence dimension, not an automatic winner-selection rule.

3.2 Fresh Model-Identity-Masked Human Evaluation¶

Development manual scores were produced separately inside the GAN and VAE notebooks. Notebook 4 therefore performs one fresh common comparison.

Generate:

  • 100 GAN images;
  • 100 VAE images;
  • 10 requested images per CIFAR-10 class per model.

The 200 images are combined and reproducibly shuffled before scoring.

Phase A: visual quality¶

During visual-quality scoring:

  • model identity is hidden;
  • requested class is hidden;
  • images are identified only by anonymous IDs.

Each image receives exactly one rating:

  • Clear
  • Marginal
  • Nonsense

Phase B: requested-class adherence¶

Requested labels are then revealed while model identity remains hidden.

Each image receives exactly one class-adherence rating:

  • Correct
  • Ambiguous
  • Incorrect

Visual quality and requested-class adherence are treated as separate judgements.

All 200 images will be scored by Rudhresh using the same predefined criteria.

The shuffled anonymous image IDs and raw ratings will be preserved so that the scoring process remains reproducible and auditable. Because Notebook 4 uses a single scorer, no inter-rater agreement statistic is reported.

This single-rater design is treated as a limitation of the manual evaluation, while model-identity masking and fixed scoring definitions reduce avoidable scoring bias.

3.3 Formal Memorisation-Audit Protocol¶

The memorisation audit asks whether generated images are unusually close to particular CIFAR-10 training examples relative to genuine unseen CIFAR-10 images.

The shared reference bank is:

  • all 50,000 CIFAR-10 training images.

The unseen-real baseline is:

  • all 10,000 CIFAR-10 test images → nearest training image.

Generated audits use:

  • 5,000 final GAN images → nearest training image;
  • 5,000 final VAE images → nearest training image.

To avoid unnecessary extra generation, the memorisation audit will reuse each model's first frozen FID generation pool, corresponding to seed 2001.

All three groups use exactly the same feature-space procedure:

  1. extract 2,048-dimensional InceptionV3 average-pooling features;
  2. L2-normalise every feature vector;
  3. use cosine distance;
  4. use the same nearest-neighbour implementation against the same training feature bank.

For each nearest-neighbour distance distribution, report:

  • median;
  • Q1 and Q3;
  • 5th percentile;
  • 1st percentile;
  • minimum;
  • mean where useful.

Also inspect:

  • the 20 closest generated-training pairs for each model;
  • unique nearest-neighbour training-image count;
  • repeated-neighbour frequency;
  • proportion of generated distances below the test-baseline 5th percentile;
  • proportion below the test-baseline 1st percentile;
  • the overall distance distributions.

Very small generated-to-training distances relative to the unseen-real baseline indicate suspicious closeness, but do not by themselves prove memorisation. The audit also cannot prove that memorisation is absent.

3.4 Protocol Freeze Statement¶

The final GAN and VAE are independently reloaded and verified, their shared RGB output contract has passed, and the complete final evaluation procedure has now been specified.

The final evaluation protocol is frozen.

From this point onward:

  • no model retraining is permitted;
  • no architecture or hyperparameter changes are permitted;
  • no checkpoint reselection is permitted;
  • no evaluation rule may be changed because of a protected-test result;
  • no additional model experiments may be introduced.

A genuine implementation error may be corrected transparently, but any affected comparison must then be rerun symmetrically.

The protected CIFAR-10 test set may now be accessed for the previously specified final evaluation only.

4. Consolidated Development Evidence¶

The final GAN and VAE were already selected and frozen inside their respective development notebooks.

This section brings forward only the evidence needed to contextualise the final cross-model comparison. No development metric is recomputed here and no earlier model-selection decision is reopened.

Development evidence remains supporting context. The final GAN-versus-VAE decision will rely primarily on the fresh common evaluation performed later in this notebook.

4.1 Final GAN Development Summary¶

The frozen GAN entering Notebook 4 is:

  • experiment: G10_conditional_fliptranslation_seed42;
  • model: conditional DCGAN;
  • selected checkpoint: epoch 100;
  • latent dimension: 100;
  • learned label-embedding dimension: 50;
  • training augmentation: horizontal flip plus two-pixel translation;
  • generator parameters: 1,290,487;
  • discriminator parameters: 675,393;
  • development FID: 34.8933 ± 0.3457;
  • requested-label agreement: 68.9%;
  • seed-42 training time: approximately 24.36 minutes;
  • independent confirmation evidence: G11_conditional_fliptranslation_seed123;
  • fresh final-weight reload verification: passed.

In the final masked G08-versus-G10 development scoring session, G10 received:

  • 55 Clear;
  • 42 Marginal;
  • 3 Nonsense.

That manual score was produced inside a GAN-only comparison session and is therefore retained as supporting development evidence rather than treated as directly comparable with the VAE's manual score.

The final GAN showed useful class control, broad predicted-class coverage and no exact duplicates in its development evaluation, although class adherence remained imperfect. In particular, requesting a class does not guarantee that every generated image clearly represents that class.

4.2 Final VAE Development Summary¶

The frozen VAE entering Notebook 4 is:

  • experiment: V04;
  • model: conditional ConvTranspose VAE;
  • selected checkpoint: epoch 50;
  • latent dimension: 64;
  • conditioning: one-hot class vector;
  • KL weight, β: 0.5;
  • reconstruction objective: L1/MAE + scaled SSIM + KL;
  • encoder parameters: 653,248;
  • decoder parameters: 394,307;
  • total parameters: 1,047,555;
  • development FID: 145.5441 ± 0.3302;
  • development manual quality: 0 Clear / 71 Marginal / 29 Nonsense;
  • requested-class agreement: 12%;
  • training time: approximately 7.77 minutes;
  • final decoder reload verification: passed.

V04's reconstruction pathway was substantially stronger than its random-generation quality. At epoch 50, deterministic reconstruction evaluation recorded approximately:

  • MSE: 0.00657;
  • MAE: 0.05792;
  • PSNR: 22.450 dB;
  • SSIM: 0.75755.

The training history reached a stable late plateau and retained finite KL behaviour rather than showing numerical divergence or an abrupt collapsed solution.

The repeated V04 development FID values were repeated generation draws from the same trained model. They therefore measure sampling variation, not independent training-seed robustness.

Most importantly for the present generative task, V04's random generations remained weakly recognisable and its requested-class control was poor despite reasonable reconstruction performance.

4.4 Model-Specific Strengths and Limitations¶

The development evidence is already strongly asymmetric, but the two model families also provide different forms of model-specific information.

GAN-specific evidence

The final GAN received independent seed-123 confirmation, adversarial-stability review, diversity and repetition safeguards, class-coverage analysis and conditional-adherence evaluation. Its main strengths were substantially stronger random-generation quality and useful requested-class control. Its main remaining weakness is that conditional adherence is still imperfect rather than deterministic.

VAE-specific evidence

The VAE provides reconstruction and latent-space diagnostics that do not have direct GAN equivalents. V04 achieved comparatively strong reconstruction metrics and stable late training behaviour, showing that it learned its reconstruction objective successfully. However, this did not translate into strong prior-sampled image generation or useful class conditioning.

These model-specific diagnostics are retained as context rather than forced into a false one-to-one comparison.

The development results therefore make the GAN the clear pre-evaluation favourite. However, the final model is not selected here. The frozen protected-test FID, fresh masked human evaluation and memorisation audit remain to be completed under the common Notebook 4 protocol.

5. One-Time Protected-Test FID¶

The final evaluation protocol is now frozen, so the official CIFAR-10 test split may be accessed for the first time in model comparison.

This section evaluates both frozen models against the same unseen real-image reference using the same InceptionV3 FID implementation.

No result produced here may be used to retrain, tune, reselect, or otherwise alter either model.

5.1 Test Reference Features¶

The real FID reference is the complete official CIFAR-10 test split of 10,000 images.

The feature pipeline is inherited from the development notebooks:

  • RGB uint8 [0,255];
  • resize from 32 × 32 to 299 × 299;
  • bilinear interpolation;
  • ImageNet InceptionV3 preprocessing;
  • ImageNet-pretrained InceptionV3;
  • global average pooling;
  • 2,048 features per image;
  • float64 feature statistics for FID.

The test-reference features are computed once and reused unchanged for every GAN and VAE repeat.

The CIFAR-10 training split is also loaded by the standard Keras dataset loader but remains unused in this FID calculation. It will later provide the fixed reference bank for the memorisation audit.

from scipy.linalg import sqrtm
from tensorflow.keras.applications import InceptionV3
from tensorflow.keras.applications.inception_v3 import preprocess_input


FID_IMAGE_SIZE = (299, 299)
FID_FEATURE_BATCH_SIZE = 64

# Extract shared 2048-D InceptionV3 features.
def extract_inception_features(
    images_uint8,
    feature_extractor,
    batch_size=FID_FEATURE_BATCH_SIZE,
):
    images_uint8 = np.asarray(images_uint8)

    assert images_uint8.ndim == 4
    assert images_uint8.shape[1:] == (32, 32, 3)
    assert images_uint8.dtype == np.uint8

    feature_batches = []

    for start in range(
        0,
        len(images_uint8),
        batch_size,
    ):
        image_batch = tf.convert_to_tensor(
            images_uint8[
                start:start + batch_size
            ],
            dtype=tf.float32,
        )

        resized_batch = tf.image.resize(
            image_batch,
            size=FID_IMAGE_SIZE,
            method="bilinear",
            antialias=False,
        )

        preprocessed_batch = preprocess_input(
            resized_batch
        )

        feature_batch = feature_extractor(
            preprocessed_batch,
            training=False,
        )

        feature_batches.append(
            feature_batch.numpy()
        )

    features = np.concatenate(
        feature_batches,
        axis=0,
    ).astype("float64")

    assert features.shape == (
        len(images_uint8),
        INCEPTION_FEATURE_DIM,
    )
    assert np.isfinite(features).all()

    return features

# Return float64 Gaussian feature statistics.
def feature_statistics(features):

    features = np.asarray(
        features,
        dtype="float64",
    )

    mean = np.mean(
        features,
        axis=0,
    )

    covariance = np.cov(
        features,
        rowvar=False,
    )

    assert mean.shape == (
        INCEPTION_FEATURE_DIM,
    )
    assert covariance.shape == (
        INCEPTION_FEATURE_DIM,
        INCEPTION_FEATURE_DIM,
    )

    return mean, covariance

# Calculate standard Frechet distance.
def frechet_distance(
    mean_1,
    covariance_1,
    mean_2,
    covariance_2,
    epsilon=1e-6,
):

    mean_1 = np.asarray(
        mean_1,
        dtype="float64",
    )
    mean_2 = np.asarray(
        mean_2,
        dtype="float64",
    )

    covariance_1 = np.asarray(
        covariance_1,
        dtype="float64",
    )
    covariance_2 = np.asarray(
        covariance_2,
        dtype="float64",
    )

    mean_difference = mean_1 - mean_2

    covariance_mean = sqrtm(
        covariance_1 @ covariance_2
    )

    if not np.isfinite(
        covariance_mean
    ).all():
        identity = (
            np.eye(
                covariance_1.shape[0]
            )
            * epsilon
        )

        covariance_mean = sqrtm(
            (covariance_1 + identity)
            @
            (covariance_2 + identity)
        )

    if np.iscomplexobj(
        covariance_mean
    ):
        maximum_imaginary = np.max(
            np.abs(
                covariance_mean.imag
            )
        )

        if maximum_imaginary > 1e-3:
            raise ValueError(
                "FID square root contains "
                "large imaginary values."
            )

        covariance_mean = (
            covariance_mean.real
        )

    fid_value = (
        mean_difference
        @ mean_difference
        + np.trace(covariance_1)
        + np.trace(covariance_2)
        - 2.0
        * np.trace(covariance_mean)
    )

    return max(
        float(fid_value),
        0.0,
    )

5.2 GAN Final FID¶

The frozen final GAN is evaluated using the three predeclared generation seeds.

For each repeat:

  • generate 5,000 images;
  • request exactly 500 images from each CIFAR-10 class;
  • convert the native [-1,1] output to shared RGB uint8 [0,255];
  • extract features using the same frozen InceptionV3 pipeline;
  • calculate FID against the single protected-test reference computed in Section 5.1.

The seed-2001 pool is retained for the later memorisation audit so that no unnecessary duplicate generation is performed.

In [13]:
# Balanced frozen-model generation helpers

FINAL_GENERATION_BATCH_SIZE = 256


def make_balanced_class_ids(
    images_per_class,
):
    class_ids = np.repeat(
        np.arange(
            NUM_CLASSES,
            dtype=np.int32,
        ),
        images_per_class,
    )

    assert len(class_ids) == (
        NUM_CLASSES * images_per_class
    )

    return class_ids


def generate_final_gan_images(
    seed,
    images_per_class,
    batch_size=FINAL_GENERATION_BATCH_SIZE,
):
    class_ids = make_balanced_class_ids(
        images_per_class
    )

    latent_vectors = tf.random.stateless_normal(
        shape=(
            len(class_ids),
            GAN_LATENT_DIM,
        ),
        seed=(seed, 0),
        dtype=tf.float32,
    )

    generated_batches = []

    for start in range(
        0,
        len(class_ids),
        batch_size,
    ):
        end = start + batch_size

        latent_batch = latent_vectors[
            start:end
        ]

        label_batch = tf.convert_to_tensor(
            class_ids[start:end].reshape(-1, 1),
            dtype=tf.int32,
        )

        native_batch = final_gan_generator(
            [
                latent_batch,
                label_batch,
            ],
            training=False,
        ).numpy()

        generated_batches.append(
            restore_from_gan(
                native_batch
            )
        )

    images_uint8 = np.concatenate(
        generated_batches,
        axis=0,
    )

    verify_shared_image_representation(
        "Final GAN generation",
        images_uint8,
    )

    assert images_uint8.shape[0] == len(
        class_ids
    )

    return images_uint8, class_ids


def generate_final_vae_images(
    seed,
    images_per_class,
    batch_size=FINAL_GENERATION_BATCH_SIZE,
):
    class_ids = make_balanced_class_ids(
        images_per_class
    )

    latent_vectors = tf.random.stateless_normal(
        shape=(
            len(class_ids),
            VAE_LATENT_DIM,
        ),
        seed=(seed, 0),
        dtype=tf.float32,
    )

    one_hot_labels = tf.one_hot(
        class_ids,
        depth=NUM_CLASSES,
        dtype=tf.float32,
    )

    generated_batches = []

    for start in range(
        0,
        len(class_ids),
        batch_size,
    ):
        end = start + batch_size

        native_batch = final_vae_decoder(
            [
                latent_vectors[start:end],
                one_hot_labels[start:end],
            ],
            training=False,
        ).numpy()

        generated_batches.append(
            restore_from_vae(
                native_batch
            )
        )

    images_uint8 = np.concatenate(
        generated_batches,
        axis=0,
    )

    verify_shared_image_representation(
        "Final VAE generation",
        images_uint8,
    )

    assert images_uint8.shape[0] == len(
        class_ids
    )

    return images_uint8, class_ids


print("Balanced generation helpers: READY")
print(
    "Generation batch size:",
    FINAL_GENERATION_BATCH_SIZE,
)

5.3 VAE Final FID¶

The frozen V04 decoder is evaluated under the identical protected-test protocol:

  • 5,000 generated images per repeat;
  • exactly 500 requested images per class;
  • the same seeds 2001, 2002, and 2003;
  • the same shared RGB representation;
  • the same frozen InceptionV3 extractor;
  • the same protected-test reference statistics;
  • the same FID implementation.

The seed-2001 VAE pool is likewise retained for the later memorisation audit.

5.4 Held-Out Comparison¶

The three repeated FID values are now compared descriptively.

Lower FID indicates that the generated feature distribution is closer to the unseen CIFAR-10 test reference under the frozen InceptionV3 representation.

The repeat standard deviation measures variation caused by different generated samples from each already-frozen model. It does not measure variation across independently trained models.

No formal cross-model FID threshold is applied. The 2.0 margin used during GAN development is not transferred to this comparison because it addressed a different source of variation.

FID is one primary final evidence source, but it does not directly measure visual recognisability, requested-class correctness, or memorisation.

5.5 Protected-Test FID Interpretation¶

The protected-test comparison strongly favours the final GAN.

Across three frozen generation repeats, the GAN achieved:

  • 36.5870
  • 36.8159
  • 36.7259

giving a mean FID of 36.7096 ± 0.1153.

The VAE achieved:

  • 147.2458
  • 146.5569
  • 147.7669

giving a mean FID of 147.1899 ± 0.6069.

The absolute difference between the two protected-test mean FIDs is 110.4803, with the GAN producing the substantially lower value.

Both models also showed relatively small variation across the three generated pools. This indicates that the observed ordering is not being driven by one unusually favourable or unfavourable generation seed. The reported standard deviations describe sampling variability from the already-frozen models and are not estimates of independent training-run uncertainty.

This protected-test result is consistent with the earlier development evidence, where the GAN also had a much lower FID than V04. However, the development and protected-test FID values should not be interpreted as directly measuring a performance increase or decrease because their real-image reference distributions differ: development evaluation used the training reference, while this final evaluation uses the previously unseen official test reference.

No statistical-significance claim or arbitrary FID decision threshold is applied. Nevertheless, the magnitude and consistency of the protected-test difference provide strong evidence that the frozen GAN's generated-image distribution is substantially closer to real CIFAR-10 than the frozen VAE's under the shared InceptionV3 representation.

FID alone does not determine the final model. The fresh blinded human evaluation and formal memorisation audit are still required before final selection.

6. Fresh Blind GAN-vs-VAE Human Evaluation¶

FID measures similarity between generated and real feature distributions, but it does not directly determine whether individual images are visually recognisable or whether requested classes are followed correctly.

A fresh common human evaluation is therefore performed using the frozen protocol from Section 3.

The comparison contains:

  • 100 GAN images;
  • 100 VAE images;
  • exactly 10 requested images per CIFAR-10 class for each model;
  • generation seed 2101;
  • reproducible blind-shuffle seed 2102.

All 200 images are scored by the same evaluator using identical criteria.

The evaluation is separated into two phases:

  1. Visual quality: Clear, Marginal, or Nonsense, without revealing either model identity or requested class.
  2. Requested-class adherence: Correct, Ambiguous, or Incorrect, after revealing the requested class while continuing to hide model identity.

Separating these judgements avoids treating a visually plausible image of the wrong class as successful conditional generation.

6.1 Anonymous Evaluation Pool and Phase A: Visual Quality¶

The two frozen models each contribute 100 balanced, uncurated samples. The 200 images are shuffled using the locked seed and identified only by anonymous IDs during visual-quality scoring. Model identity and requested class remain concealed while Clear, Marginal and Nonsense ratings are recorded and frozen.

def show_blind_evaluation_page(
    images,
    blind_ids,
    page,
    images_per_page=50,
):
    start = page * images_per_page
    end = min(
        start + images_per_page,
        len(images),
    )

    page_images = images[start:end]
    page_ids = blind_ids[start:end]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        5,
        10,
        figsize=(15, 8),
    )

    axes = axes.flatten()

    for ax, image, blind_id in zip(
        axes,
        page_images,
        page_ids,
    ):
        ax.imshow(image)
        ax.set_title(
            blind_id,
            fontsize=8,
        )
        ax.axis("off")

    for ax in axes[len(page_images):]:
        ax.axis("off")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

6.2 Phase B: Requested-Class Adherence¶

Phase A visual-quality ratings are now frozen.

For Phase B, the requested CIFAR-10 class is revealed for each anonymous image while model identity remains hidden.

Each image receives exactly one adherence rating:

  • Correct: the requested class is clearly the most defensible interpretation.
  • Ambiguous: the requested class is plausible, but the visual evidence is weak or another class is also reasonably plausible.
  • Incorrect: the image more strongly resembles another class, or provides no meaningful evidence for the requested class.

This judgement is separate from visual quality. A low-quality image may still show some requested-class structure, while a visually recognisable image may depict the wrong requested class.

def show_phase_b_page(
    images,
    blind_ids,
    requested_classes,
    page,
    images_per_page=50,
):
    start = page * images_per_page
    end = min(
        start + images_per_page,
        len(images),
    )

    page_images = images[start:end]
    page_ids = blind_ids[start:end]
    page_classes = requested_classes[start:end]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        5,
        10,
        figsize=(15, 9),
    )

    axes = axes.flatten()

    for ax, image, blind_id, requested_class in zip(
        axes,
        page_images,
        page_ids,
        page_classes,
    ):
        ax.imshow(image)

        ax.set_title(
            f"{blind_id}\n{requested_class}",
            fontsize=8,
        )

        ax.axis("off")

    for ax in axes[len(page_images):]:
        ax.axis("off")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

6.3 Unmasked Human-Evaluation Results¶

Both scoring phases were completed and frozen before model identity was revealed.

The anonymous image IDs are now mapped back to their source models. This allows visual quality and requested-class adherence to be compared between the frozen GAN and VAE without changing any individual rating after unmasking.

Because each model contributed exactly 100 images, counts can also be interpreted directly as percentages.

6.4 Blind Human-Evaluation Interpretation¶

The fresh masked human evaluation strongly favours the GAN.

After model identity was revealed, the GAN accounted for all 50 Clear-rated images, giving 50% Clear, 45% Marginal and 5% Nonsense. The VAE produced 0% Clear, 71% Marginal and 29% Nonsense.

Requested-class adherence showed an even larger difference. The GAN received 48 Correct, 30 Ambiguous and 22 Incorrect ratings, while the VAE received only 1 Correct, 65 Ambiguous and 34 Incorrect.

These scores were fixed before model identity was revealed, so the model comparison did not influence the individual ratings.

The adherence result also shows why conditional generation quality should not be assessed using image quality alone. Some generated images contained plausible object structure but did not convincingly represent the requested class.

The GAN's strongest fresh class-control results were for automobiles, ships and horses, while frogs, birds and dogs were more difficult in this 10-image-per-class sample. These class-level results are descriptive because each class contains only ten images.

The fresh human evidence therefore agrees with the protected-test FID result: the GAN is substantially stronger than V04 for the image-generation objective. However, final model selection remains deferred until the formal memorisation audit is completed.

A limitation is that the manual evaluation used one scorer. Model-identity masking, fixed criteria and freezing ratings before unmasking reduce avoidable bias, but they do not eliminate scorer subjectivity.

7. Formal Memorisation Audit¶

FID evaluates overall feature-distribution similarity, but does not determine whether individual generated images are unusually close to particular training examples.

The final memorisation audit therefore compares nearest-training-image distances for three groups:

  • all 10,000 unseen CIFAR-10 test images;
  • 5,000 frozen GAN images from final FID seed 2001;
  • 5,000 frozen VAE images from final FID seed 2001.

All groups use the same 50,000 CIFAR-10 training images as the reference bank.

The previously frozen protocol uses:

  • the same InceptionV3 average-pooling features used for FID;
  • 2,048 features per image;
  • L2-normalised feature vectors;
  • cosine distance;
  • one identical exact nearest-neighbour procedure for test, GAN and VAE.

The official test-to-training distribution provides a natural unseen-real baseline. Generated images that are substantially closer to the training set than genuine unseen images warrant closer inspection, but unusually small distance alone does not prove memorisation.

7.1 Training Feature Bank¶

The full 50,000-image CIFAR-10 training set is passed through the same frozen InceptionV3 feature extractor already used in Section 5.

This feature bank represents the images that were available during model training.

No model inference, tuning or training occurs in this step.

7.2 Shared Cosine-Distance Representation¶

Raw Inception features are L2-normalised before nearest-neighbour comparison.

For two L2-normalised feature vectors, cosine distance is:

1 − cosine similarity

Lower distance means greater feature-space similarity.

The same exact implementation is used for the unseen-real baseline and both generated-image groups.

In [40]:
# L2-normalised feature representation

def l2_normalise_features(features):
    features = np.asarray(
        features,
        dtype=np.float32,
    )

    norms = np.linalg.norm(
        features,
        axis=1,
        keepdims=True,
    )

    assert np.all(norms > 0.0)

    normalised = features / norms

    assert np.isfinite(normalised).all()

    return normalised.astype(
        np.float32,
        copy=False,
    )


train_nn_features = l2_normalise_features(
    train_inception_features
)

test_nn_features = l2_normalise_features(
    test_inception_features
)

gan_nn_features = l2_normalise_features(
    gan_memorisation_features
)

vae_nn_features = l2_normalise_features(
    vae_memorisation_features
)

In [42]:
# Exact nearest-training-neighbour search

NN_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE = 256

# Exact nearest neighbours for L2-normalised features.
# For normalised vectors:
# cosine distance = 1 - dot product

# Returns:
# nearest_distances
# nearest_reference_indices
def exact_cosine_nearest_neighbours(
    query_features,
    reference_features,
    batch_size=NN_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE,
):

    query_features = np.asarray(
        query_features,
        dtype=np.float32,
    )

    reference_features = np.asarray(
        reference_features,
        dtype=np.float32,
    )

    assert query_features.ndim == 2
    assert reference_features.ndim == 2

    assert (
        query_features.shape[1]
        == reference_features.shape[1]
        == INCEPTION_FEATURE_DIM
    )

    reference_tensor = tf.convert_to_tensor(
        reference_features,
        dtype=tf.float32,
    )

    all_distances = []
    all_indices = []

    for start in range(
        0,
        len(query_features),
        batch_size,
    ):
        end = min(
            start + batch_size,
            len(query_features),
        )

        query_tensor = tf.convert_to_tensor(
            query_features[start:end],
            dtype=tf.float32,
        )

        similarities = tf.linalg.matmul(
            query_tensor,
            reference_tensor,
            transpose_b=True,
        )

        nearest_similarity = tf.reduce_max(
            similarities,
            axis=1,
        )

        nearest_index = tf.argmax(
            similarities,
            axis=1,
            output_type=tf.int32,
        )

        nearest_distance = (
            1.0 - nearest_similarity
        )

        nearest_distance = tf.clip_by_value(
            nearest_distance,
            0.0,
            2.0,
        )

        all_distances.append(
            nearest_distance.numpy()
        )

        all_indices.append(
            nearest_index.numpy()
        )

        del similarities

    distances = np.concatenate(
        all_distances
    ).astype(np.float32)

    indices = np.concatenate(
        all_indices
    ).astype(np.int32)

    assert distances.shape == (
        len(query_features),
    )

    assert indices.shape == (
        len(query_features),
    )

    assert np.isfinite(distances).all()

    return distances, indices


print(
    "Exact cosine nearest-neighbour search: READY"
)
print(
    "Query batch size:",
    NN_QUERY_BATCH_SIZE,
)

7.3 Test-to-Training Baseline¶

The complete official test set is first compared with the training feature bank.

This provides the reference distribution for how close genuine unseen CIFAR-10 images naturally lie to the training set.

7.4 GAN- and VAE-to-Training Distances¶

The retained seed-2001 GAN and VAE generation pools are then evaluated using exactly the same nearest-neighbour procedure.

In [43]:

# GAN  -> training
# VAE  -> training

(
    test_to_train_distances,
    test_to_train_indices,
) = exact_cosine_nearest_neighbours(
    test_nn_features,
    train_nn_features,

7.5 Nearest-Neighbour Distance Summary¶

The nearest-training-image distance distributions are summarised using the mean, median, interquartile range and lower-tail percentiles.

The lower tail is especially relevant because potential memorisation would appear as generated images lying unusually close to particular training examples.

Rather than introducing an arbitrary similarity threshold, the unseen-real test distribution provides the baseline. The proportions of GAN and VAE samples falling at or below the test-set 5th and 1st percentile distances are therefore reported directly.

A generated distribution that is substantially shifted toward smaller distances than the test baseline would warrant closer inspection.

In [44]:
# Distance-distribution summaries

def summarise_nn_distances(
    group_name,
    distances,
):
    distances = np.asarray(
        distances,
        dtype=np.float64,
    )

    return {
        "Group": group_name,
        "N": len(distances),
        "Mean": np.mean(distances),
        "Median": np.median(distances),
        "Q1": np.percentile(
            distances,
            25,
        ),
        "Q3": np.percentile(
            distances,
            75,
        ),
        "5th percentile": np.percentile(
            distances,
            5,
        ),
        "1st percentile": np.percentile(
            distances,
            1,
        ),
        "Minimum": np.min(distances),
    }

            "Test -> training",
            test_to_train_distances,

            "GAN -> training",
            gan_to_train_distances,
        ),
        summarise_nn_distances(
            "VAE -> training",
            vae_to_train_distances,

    ]
)

):

            <= threshold

7.6 Nearest-Training-Image Reuse¶

Nearest-neighbour distance alone does not show whether many generated images repeatedly map to the same training examples.

This section therefore measures:

  • the number of unique training images selected as nearest neighbours;
  • duplicate nearest-neighbour assignments;
  • how many training images are reused at least twice;
  • the maximum number of generated images assigned to any single training neighbour.

High reuse does not by itself demonstrate memorisation. In particular, repeated assignment can also reflect low generated diversity or concentration around a limited set of visual modes.

The reuse results are therefore interpreted together with the actual nearest-neighbour distances and later visual inspection of the closest pairs.

In [45]:
# Nearest-training-image reuse

def summarise_neighbour_reuse(
    group_name,
    neighbour_indices,
):
    neighbour_indices = np.asarray(
        neighbour_indices
    )

    unique_indices, counts = np.unique(
        neighbour_indices,
        return_counts=True,
    )

    duplicate_assignments = (
        len(neighbour_indices)
        - len(unique_indices)
    )

    return {
        "Group": group_name,
        "Queries": len(neighbour_indices),
        "Unique training neighbours": (
            len(unique_indices)
        ),
        "Duplicate assignments": (
            duplicate_assignments
        ),
        "Duplicate-assignment %": (
            duplicate_assignments
            / len(neighbour_indices)
            * 100
        ),
        "Training neighbours reused >=2 times": int(
            np.sum(counts >= 2)
        ),
        "Maximum reuse count": int(
            np.max(counts)
        ),
    }


neighbour_reuse_table = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        summarise_neighbour_reuse(
            "Test baseline",
            test_to_train_indices,
        ),
        summarise_neighbour_reuse(
            "GAN",
            gan_to_train_indices,
        ),
        summarise_neighbour_reuse(
            "VAE",
            vae_to_train_indices,
        ),
    ]
)

display(

7.7 Nearest-Neighbour Distance Distribution¶

An empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) provides a direct visual comparison of the complete nearest-training-distance distributions.

For any cosine-distance value on the horizontal axis, the vertical axis shows the proportion of images whose nearest training example lies at or below that distance.

A curve shifted further left indicates generally smaller nearest-training distances.

The official test-to-training curve acts as the unseen-real reference. The generated distributions are interpreted relative to this baseline rather than against an arbitrary absolute distance threshold.

In [46]:
# Nearest-neighbour distance ECDF

def ecdf(values):
    values = np.sort(
        np.asarray(values)
    )

    probabilities = (
        np.arange(
            1,
            len(values) + 1,
        )
        / len(values)
    )

    return values, probabilities


plt.figure(
    figsize=(8, 5)
)

for label, distances in [
    (
        "Test -> training",
        test_to_train_distances,
    ),
    (
        "GAN -> training",
        gan_to_train_distances,
    ),
    (
        "VAE -> training",
        vae_to_train_distances,
    ),
]:
    x, y = ecdf(
        distances
    )

    plt.plot(
        x,
        y,
        label=label,
    )

plt.xlabel(
    "Nearest-training cosine distance"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Cumulative proportion"
)

plt.title(
    "Nearest-Training-Image Distance ECDF"
)

plt.legend()

plt.grid(
    alpha=0.25
)

plt.show()

7.8 Distribution-Level Memorisation Findings¶

The distribution-level results do not indicate suspicious training-set proximity for either frozen generator.

The unseen-real CIFAR-10 test images were naturally closer to the training set than either generated group. Their median nearest-training cosine distance was 0.149454, compared with 0.185561 for the GAN and 0.177739 for the VAE.

The lower tail provides even stronger evidence. The test baseline 5th-percentile distance was 0.074740 and its 1st-percentile distance was 0.042734. None of the 5,000 GAN samples and none of the 5,000 VAE samples fell at or below either threshold.

The nearest-neighbour reuse results reveal a separate difference in diversity. The GAN's 5,000 samples mapped to 3,595 unique training neighbours, whereas the VAE mapped to only 1,006. The VAE also showed a much larger duplicate-assignment rate (79.88%) and maximum reuse count (124) than the GAN (28.10% and 22 respectively).

Because the VAE's nearest-neighbour distances are not unusually small, this high reuse is more consistent with generated-image concentration or limited diversity than with direct training-image memorisation.

These distribution-level findings are reassuring, but the closest generated-training pairs are still inspected visually before the memorisation audit is concluded.

7.9 Closest Generated–Training Pair Inspection¶

The distribution-level audit found no generated samples below the unseen-real test baseline's 5th- or 1st-percentile nearest-neighbour distances.

As a final qualitative check, the 20 generated images with the smallest training-set cosine distances are inspected for each model.

Each displayed pair contains:

  • the generated image;
  • its exact nearest training image under the frozen feature-space search;
  • the cosine distance between them;
  • the requested generated class;
  • the true CIFAR-10 class of the nearest training image.

Visual resemblance is interpreted cautiously. Similar pose, colour, background, or object structure can produce close feature-space matches without implying that an image was copied.

A close-looking pair is therefore supporting evidence only. Memorisation would be more concerning if the generated image reproduced unusually specific training-image content and also showed abnormally small feature distance relative to the unseen-real baseline.

In [48]:
# 20 closest generated -> training pairs per model

CLOSEST_PAIR_COUNT = 20

gan_closest_generated_indices = np.argsort(
    gan_to_train_distances
)[:CLOSEST_PAIR_COUNT]

vae_closest_generated_indices = np.argsort(
    vae_to_train_distances
)[:CLOSEST_PAIR_COUNT]


def build_closest_pair_table(
    model_name,
    generated_indices,
    nearest_training_indices,
    distances,
    requested_classes,
):
    rows = []

    for rank, generated_index in enumerate(
        generated_indices,
        start=1,
    ):
        training_index = int(
            nearest_training_indices[
                generated_index
            ]
        )

        requested_class_id = int(
            requested_classes[
                generated_index
            ]
        )

        training_class_id = int(
            cifar10_train_labels[
                training_index
            ].reshape(-1)[0]
        )

        rows.append(
            {
                "Rank": rank,
                "Model": model_name,
                "Generated index": int(
                    generated_index
                ),
                "Requested class": (
                    CLASS_NAMES[
                        requested_class_id
                    ]
                ),
                "Nearest training index": (
                    training_index
                ),
                "Training class": (
                    CLASS_NAMES[
                        training_class_id
                    ]
                ),
                "Cosine distance": float(
                    distances[
                        generated_index
                    ]
                ),
            }
        )

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

# Closest-pair visual inspection

def show_closest_pair_grid(
    generated_images,
    pair_table,
    title,
):
    pairs_per_row = 5
    rows = 4

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        rows,
        pairs_per_row * 2,
        figsize=(16, 9),
    )

    axes = np.asarray(axes)

    for pair_position, row in (
        pair_table.reset_index(
            drop=True
        ).iterrows()
    ):
        grid_row = (
            pair_position
            // pairs_per_row
        )

        pair_column = (
            pair_position
            % pairs_per_row
        )

        generated_axis = axes[
            grid_row,
            pair_column * 2,
        ]

        training_axis = axes[
            grid_row,
            pair_column * 2 + 1,
        ]

        generated_index = int(
            row["Generated index"]
        )

        training_index = int(
            row["Nearest training index"]
        )

        distance = float(
            row["Cosine distance"]
        )

        generated_axis.imshow(
            generated_images[
                generated_index
            ]
        )

        generated_axis.set_title(
            (
                f"#{int(row['Rank']):02d} Generated\n"
                f"Req: {row['Requested class']}\n"
                f"d={distance:.4f}"
            ),
            fontsize=8,
        )

        generated_axis.axis("off")

        training_axis.imshow(
            cifar10_train_images[
                training_index
            ]
        )

        training_axis.set_title(
            (
                "Nearest train\n"
                f"True: {row['Training class']}"
            ),
            fontsize=8,
        )

        training_axis.axis("off")

    fig.suptitle(
        title,
        fontsize=14,
        y=1.01,
    )

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

7.10 Memorisation Audit Conclusion¶

The formal nearest-neighbour audit found no concerning evidence of direct training-image memorisation for either frozen model.

Genuine unseen CIFAR-10 test images were naturally closer to the training set than either generated group: the median nearest-training cosine distance was 0.149454 for the test baseline, compared with 0.185561 for the GAN and 0.177739 for the VAE. None of the 5,000 samples from either generator fell below the test baseline's 5th- or 1st-percentile distance thresholds, and visual inspection of the closest generated–training pairs showed no obvious direct reproductions.

The main difference instead concerned diversity. The GAN's samples mapped to 3,595 unique training neighbours, whereas the VAE mapped to only 1,006. Because the VAE's distances were not unusually small, this concentration is more consistent with repeated visual modes and weaker generated diversity than with copying specific training examples.

This audit cannot prove that memorisation is absent, but it provides no evidence that the GAN's stronger final performance is explained by direct reproduction of the training set.

8. Final GAN-versus-VAE Selection¶

All frozen final evaluations are now complete:

  • protected-test FID;
  • fresh blinded visual-quality scoring;
  • fresh blinded requested-class adherence;
  • formal training-set memorisation audit.

The final model is selected using the complete evidence rather than a weighted composite score or a single automatic decision rule.

8.2 Veto Check¶

Before choosing the stronger model, each finalist is checked for any serious failure that would invalidate selection.

Potential vetoes include:

  • failure to reload the frozen artifact;
  • invalid inference output;
  • protected-test leakage during development;
  • missing required final model artifacts;
  • severe unresolved memorisation concern;
  • evidence that the model cannot support the required ten-class submission procedure.

Neither model currently triggers a veto.

Both frozen generation artifacts reload successfully and produce valid 32 × 32 × 3 RGB outputs. The protected test set remained unused during model development, and the formal nearest-neighbour audit found no suspicious training-set proximity for either model.

The GAN's requested-class adherence is imperfect, so requesting a class does not guarantee that every generated image will be semantically correct. This is an operational limitation rather than a veto because the model still provides measurable and substantially stronger conditional control than the VAE.

For the final 1,000-image deliverable, the class-labelled filenames represent the conditioning requests supplied to the frozen GAN rather than verified semantic correctness for every individual image. This limitation is disclosed explicitly and has already been quantified through the development and fresh blinded adherence evaluations.

8.3 Quality, Diversity and Control Trade-Off¶

The final comparison is not close.

The GAN achieved a protected-test FID of 36.7096 ± 0.1153, compared with 147.1899 ± 0.6069 for the VAE. The approximately 110.48-point mean difference is consistent with the much smaller development FID observed for the GAN.

The fresh blinded human evaluation reaches the same conclusion. The GAN produced 50% Clear images and only 5% Nonsense images, whereas the VAE produced no Clear images and 29% Nonsense images.

Conditional control also strongly favours the GAN. 48% of its fresh images were rated Correct for their requested class, compared with only 1% for the VAE. The GAN is still imperfect, particularly for classes such as frog, bird and dog, but its conditioning is operationally useful in a way that V04's conditioning is not.

The memorisation audit does not reveal a hidden cost that overturns these results. Neither model produced unusually close training-set matches relative to the unseen-real baseline. The VAE instead showed substantially greater nearest-neighbour reuse, with 79.88% duplicate assignments compared with 28.10% for the GAN. Because the VAE distances were not abnormally small, this is more consistent with limited generative diversity than training-image copying.

Overall, the GAN has the substantially stronger combination of image quality, distributional realism, conditional control and generated diversity.

8.4 Stability, Compute and Reproducibility¶

The VAE retains two clear practical advantages: it is smaller and faster to train.

The frozen VAE decoder contains 394,307 parameters, compared with 1,290,487 parameters in the GAN generator. Representative V04 training took approximately 7.77 minutes, while the final GAN seed-42 run took approximately 24.36 minutes.

The VAE also provides a useful reconstruction pathway that the GAN does not. Its deterministic reconstruction metrics showed that it learned the reconstruction objective substantially better than its random generations might suggest.

However, these advantages do not compensate for the very large gap in the actual assignment objective of generating recognisable CIFAR-10 images.

Reproducibility evidence is satisfactory for both models because their frozen generation artifacts were independently reloaded successfully in this notebook. Robustness evidence is somewhat stronger for the GAN because its final configuration was additionally confirmed with an independent seed-123 training run. The VAE's repeated FID values came from repeated generation draws from one trained model and should not be interpreted as equivalent training-seed evidence.

8.5 Overall Winner¶

Overall selected model: GAN

The final conditional GAN is selected as the overall model for the official 1,000-image submission.

The decision is decisive rather than close.

The strongest reasons are:

  1. substantially lower protected-test FID;
  2. substantially stronger blinded visual quality and recognisability;
  3. substantially stronger requested-class adherence;
  4. broader generated-image coverage;
  5. independent training-seed confirmation;
  6. no evidence that its stronger performance is explained by suspicious training-image memorisation.

The VAE is computationally cheaper, has fewer generation-network parameters and provides a useful reconstruction pathway. These are meaningful advantages, but they do not outweigh its weak prior-sampled image quality, near-absent requested-class control and stronger evidence of generated-mode concentration.

The main residual limitation of the selected GAN is imperfect conditional adherence. Therefore, the class names used for the final 1,000-image set represent the conditioning requests supplied to the generator rather than a guarantee that every individual output is semantically correct. This limitation has already been quantified through the frozen development and fresh blinded adherence evaluations.

9. Assignment-Specific Final Analysis¶

The final model comparison is complete and the GAN has been selected and frozen.

This section answers the remaining assignment-specific questions directly by synthesising evidence from the earlier notebooks and the final Notebook 4 evaluation.

No new model training or tuning is performed.

9.1 Requested-Class Generation¶

Both final model families implemented conditional generation, but their class-control reliability differed substantially.

The final GAN accepts:

  • a latent vector of dimension 100; and
  • an integer requested-class label with shape (N,1).

The requested label is mapped through a learned embedding and concatenated with the latent vector before image generation.

The final VAE accepts:

  • a latent vector of dimension 64; and
  • a one-hot requested-class vector with shape (N,10).

The class vector is concatenated with the latent representation before decoding.

A conditional input does not guarantee that the generated image will semantically match the requested class. The model learns a statistical relationship between labels and image structure rather than a deterministic class-rendering rule.

This limitation was measurable.

During development, the frozen-classifier requested-label agreement was:

  • GAN: 68.9%;
  • VAE: 12%.

The fresh strict human evaluation in Notebook 4 found:

  • GAN: 48 Correct / 30 Ambiguous / 22 Incorrect;
  • VAE: 1 Correct / 65 Ambiguous / 34 Incorrect.

The GAN therefore provides useful direct requested-class control, while the VAE's conditioning was too weak for reliable final class-specific generation.

For the official submission, the selected GAN requests each target class directly to produce 100 requested samples per class. The class label records the conditioning request rather than guaranteeing semantic correctness for every individual image. This limitation has already been quantified through the development and fresh blinded adherence evaluations.

9.2 Easier and Harder CIFAR-10 Classes¶

Notebook 1 proposed that classes with more consistent global structure, particularly some vehicle classes, might be easier to generate, while animal classes could be harder because of greater variation in pose, texture and background.

The final answer is based on generated-image evidence rather than the EDA hypothesis alone.

The fresh Notebook 4 evaluation used exactly ten requested images per class for each model. These counts are descriptive rather than precise class-success estimates because the per-class sample size is small.

The final GAN results partly confirm the original EDA hypothesis.

Relatively easier classes

  • Automobile: 10/10 Correct;
  • Ship: 8/10;
  • Horse: 7/10.

Automobiles and ships have relatively distinctive large-scale silhouettes and commonly appear against visually consistent road, sky or water backgrounds. Horse generation also performed strongly in this final sample, showing that the vehicle-versus-animal distinction is not absolute.

Moderate classes

  • Airplane: 5/10;
  • Deer: 5/10;
  • Truck: 5/10.

These classes showed useful conditioning but less consistent recognisability.

Relatively harder classes

  • Cat: 3/10;
  • Bird: 2/10;
  • Dog: 2/10;
  • Frog: 1/10.

These classes generally contain more variable poses, textures and backgrounds and can be visually similar to other animal classes at CIFAR-10's 32 × 32 resolution. The frog condition was also the weakest class during the GAN's earlier development evaluation, so its difficulty was not unique to the final Notebook 4 sample.

The VAE does not provide a useful class-difficulty ranking because only one of its 100 fresh samples was rated Correct, a Ship image. Its dominant limitation is therefore weak class conditioning overall rather than a reliable distinction between easier and harder classes.

These results describe observed model behaviour rather than proving that a particular visual property causes a class to be easy or difficult.

9.3 RGB versus Grayscale Generation¶

Reducing CIFAR-10 from RGB to grayscale changes the generation problem in two opposing ways.

Grayscale removes two colour channels and therefore reduces the amount of information the generator and discriminator must model. This can simplify optimisation and allow the network to focus more strongly on object structure, edges and luminance.

However, colour is useful information in CIFAR-10. Removing it eliminates cues that help distinguish objects, materials and backgrounds, and a structurally cleaner grayscale image is not automatically a better semantic image.

Notebook 2 tested this directly using one controlled grayscale GAN:

G12_grayscale_fliptranslation_seed42

The grayscale experiment used the final improved unconditional settings, one fresh seed and a fair grayscale-transformed real reference.

Its selected epoch-100 checkpoint achieved:

  • repeated grayscale-reference FID: 22.0720 ± 0.1403;
  • manual quality: 40 Clear / 51 Marginal / 9 Nonsense;
  • +18 Clear images relative to the matched RGB manual comparison;
  • diversity ratio: 0.907328 ± 0.009765;
  • exact duplicates: 0.

The grayscale and RGB FID values are not directly ranked because they use different real-image reference distributions.

The controlled experiment nevertheless showed that structural generation was easier in grayscale for this DCGAN. Removing colour allowed substantially more outputs to exhibit recognisable object structure.

That structural improvement did not make grayscale preferable overall. Colour cues were lost and feature-space diversity was moderately reduced. Since the assignment concerns the original colour CIFAR-10 task, the grayscale model remained a discussion-only sensitivity experiment rather than a finalist.

No separate grayscale VAE was trained. Notebook 3 reasoned that grayscale would probably also simplify the VAE task because removing colour reduces channel-to-channel variation, but this was not tested experimentally and is therefore treated as a hypothesis rather than a finding.

Therefore, the two model families are not equally evidenced on this question. The GAN conclusion is supported by a controlled grayscale training experiment, whereas the VAE discussion remains reasoned model-family speculation. Whether the same magnitude of benefit would occur for the VAE remains unresolved.

The final conclusion is therefore:

For the tested DCGAN, grayscale generation was easier for producing recognisable structure, but easier optimisation did not equal better overall CIFAR-10 generation because useful colour information was removed. A similar simplification is plausible for the VAE, but was not experimentally tested in this project.

No additional grayscale VAE is trained in Notebook 4 because both model-development tracks are already frozen.

9.4 Augmentation Findings¶

Notebook 1 identified horizontal flips and small translations as plausible CIFAR-10 augmentations because they can add positional variation without strongly changing object identity.

Notebook 2 then investigated augmentation empirically rather than assuming that it would help.

The final retained policy was:

  • horizontal flip with probability 0.5;
  • translation of at most two pixels along each spatial axis;
  • reflection filling.

Augmentation was applied dynamically during adversarial training and was not applied to FID evaluation or ordinary generated-image evaluation.

The initial unconditional augmentation study found favourable but relatively modest evidence for flip plus translation. The more important final test occurred after class conditioning was introduced.

A focused conditional ablation compared:

  • augmented G10/G11;
  • matched no-augmentation G13/G14.

At training seed 42, augmentation made almost no measurable FID difference:

  • augmented G10: 34.8933 ± 0.3457;
  • no-augmentation G13: 34.6523 ± 0.7505.

The 0.2410 difference was well inside the predeclared 2.0 practical margin and was therefore a practical tie.

The independent seed-123 confirmation changed the conclusion:

  • augmented G11 remained stable at approximately 35.2332 FID;
  • no-augmentation G14 deteriorated to 109.2491 ± 0.2793.

Across the two matched training seeds:

  • augmented mean FID: 35.0633;
  • no-augmentation mean FID: 71.9507.

The no-augmentation seed-123 run also showed severe within-class feature-space diversity collapse, while the augmented counterpart remained stable.

Therefore, flip plus translation augmentation was retained for the final conditional GAN.

The result should still be interpreted cautiously. Seed 42 showed that augmentation is not guaranteed to improve every individual run, while the seed-123 comparison showed that it can provide important robustness against a severe failure mode. Two training seeds are not sufficient to establish how frequently this protective effect would occur.

The final conclusion is:

For the final conditional DCGAN, mild spatial augmentation was beneficial overall because the augmented configuration remained stable across the two tested seeds, while one matched no-augmentation confirmation run suffered severe diversity collapse.

The final VAE used no augmentation throughout its controlled experiments, so no VAE augmentation benefit is claimed.

10. Official 1,000-Image Generation¶

The overall model decision is frozen. The selected conditional GAN is now used to create the assignment's final image deliverable:

10 classes × 100 requested samples = 1,000 images

This stage is final output generation only. It does not alter the model, weights, architecture, conditioning method or evaluation protocol.

10.1 Final Generation Procedure¶

The frozen final GAN is used to generate exactly 100 requested samples for each of the ten CIFAR-10 classes, producing 1,000 images in total.

A fixed deterministic seed policy is used so that the complete output set can be reproduced.

Each generated image is converted from the GAN's native [-1,1] output to RGB uint8 [0,255] and saved as an individual PNG file using the naming convention:

<class>_<001-100>.png

Examples:

  • airplane_001.png
  • automobile_001.png
  • frog_100.png
  • truck_100.png

All images are stored directly inside one final_1000_images folder.

No post-generation quality filtering or cherry-picking is performed. The final audit checks the exact file count, per-class count, image dimensions, RGB format, readability, filename pattern and accidental exact duplicates.
